variables.title: Definitions & Let
variables.code:
x : Nat
x = 42

-- Local definition with let
result : Nat
result = let y = 10 in x + y
variables.notes: Values in Agda are immutable equations. Definitions require explicit type signatures.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
data Bool : Set where
  true  : Bool
  false : Bool

data Nat : Set where
  zero : Nat
  suc  : Nat -> Nat
data_types.notes: Types are defined using inductive data types with explicitly typed constructors.

operators.title: Mixfix Operators
operators.code:
_+_ : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
zero    + n = n
(suc m) + n = suc (m + n)

infixl 6 _+_
operators.notes: Agda supports arbitrary mixfix operators where underscores designate operand positions.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
if_then_else_ : {A : Set} -> Bool -> A -> A -> A
if true  then t else f = t
if false then t else f = f

status : String
status = if true then "active" else "idle"
conditionals.notes: Conditionals are typically user-defined mixfix functions that pattern match on boolean constructors.

for_loop.title: Recursion
for_loop.code:
map : {A B : Set} -> (A -> B) -> List A -> List B
map f []       = []
map f (x :: xs) = f x :: map f xs
for_loop.notes: Agda has no loops; structural recursion over inductive structures is verified to terminate by the totality checker.

while_loop.title: Totality & Well-Founded Recursion
while_loop.code:
-- Unbounded while loops are prohibited in total Agda.
-- Computations must provide a proof of termination.
while_loop.notes: General while loops cannot exist without fuel or coinductive/well-founded termination proofs.

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
double : Nat -> Nat
double zero    = zero
double (suc n) = suc (suc (double n))

-- Dependent function
replicate : (n : Nat) -> {A : Set} -> A -> Vec A n
functions.notes: Functions are first-class, pure, and can have dependent types where return types depend on input values.

arrays.title: Vectors (Length-Indexed)
arrays.code:
data Vec (A : Set) : Nat -> Set where
  []   : Vec A zero
  _::_ : {n : Nat} -> A -> Vec A n -> Vec A (suc n)
arrays.notes: Length-indexed vectors guarantee out-of-bounds errors are caught statically at compile time.

maps.title: Association Lists / Finite Maps
maps.code:
lookup : {A B : Set} -> DecEq A -> A -> List (A * B) -> Maybe B
lookup _    k [] = nothing
lookup deq k ((k' , v) :: rest) = if deq k k' then just v else lookup deq k rest
maps.notes: Maps are represented as key-value association lists or verified balanced trees.

error_handling.title: Maybe & Proof of Validity
error_handling.code:
data Maybe (A : Set) : Set where
  just    : A -> Maybe A
  nothing : Maybe A

safeDiv : Nat -> (d : Nat) -> {p : NonZero d} -> Nat
error_handling.notes: Errors are handled using Maybe/Either or ruled out entirely by requiring proofs as function parameters.

comments.title: Comments & Annotations
comments.code:
-- Single-line comment
{- Multi-line
   comment block -}
add :: Int -> Int -> Int
add a b = a + b
comments.notes: Agda uses functional comment delimiters (-- in Haskell/ML, ; in Lisps, # or % in BEAM).

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.code:
x = 42 :: Int
big = 100000000000000000000 :: Integer
piVal = 3.14159 :: Double
hexVal = 0xFF
numbers.notes: Agda supports exact rational fractions, arbitrary-precision integers, and IEEE floats natively.

booleans.title: Booleans & Logic
booleans.code:
isActive = True
isDone = False
result = isActive && not isDone
booleans.notes: Agda treats booleans as first-class algebraic constructors (True/False, true/false, t/nil).

type_casting.title: Type Conversion
type_casting.code:
intVal = 42 :: Int
floatVal = fromIntegral intVal :: Double
strVal = show intVal
parsed = read "123" :: Int
type_casting.notes: Agda performs conversion via typeclass methods (fromIntegral, show, read) or explicit parse functions.

strings.title: Strings & Text
strings.notes: Agda represents strings as linked lists of characters, UTF-8 binaries, or dedicated text buffers.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.code:
import Text.Printf
msg = printf "User %s scored %d" "Alice" (95 :: Int)
string_formatting.notes: Agda formats text through format strings, interpolation macros, or string concatenation.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching
pattern_matching.code:
describeList xs = case xs of
    []       -> "Empty list"
    [x]      -> "Single element"
    (x:y:_)  -> "Multiple elements"
pattern_matching.notes: Pattern matching is a core feature in Agda, destructuring algebraic variants, tuples, and lists directly.

range.title: Ranges & Sequences
range.code:
-- Infinite lazy sequence
evens = [0, 2 .. 20]
-- List slice with take/drop
sub = take 5 (drop 2 [1..10])
range.notes: Agda constructs ranges as lazy lists, infinite streams, or structured range enumerables.

iterators.title: Iterators & Comprehensions
iterators.code:
-- List comprehension
squares = [x * x | x <- [1..10], even x]
iterators.notes: Agda achieves iterative processing through list comprehensions, map/filter transforms, and recursion.

oop_classes.title: Types & Abstractions (OOP Equivalent)
oop_classes.notes: Agda emphasizes algebraic data types, protocols/typeclasses, and structs over traditional class hierarchies.

lists.title: Lists (Linked Lists)
lists.code:
list = [1, 2, 3]
appended = 0 : list  -- Cons: O(1)
merged = list ++ [4, 5] -- Concat
lists.notes: Lists in Agda are singly linked immutable sequences optimized for head/tail structural sharing.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Agda uses fixed-length heterogeneous tuples for bundling related data points and function return values.

sets.title: Sets
sets.code:
import qualified Data.Set as Set
s = Set.fromList [1, 2, 3]
s' = Set.insert 4 s
exists = Set.member 2 s'
sets.notes: Agda provides persistent immutable sets implemented via balanced binary trees (HAMT / AVL).

modules_import.title: Modules & Imports
modules_import.notes: Agda isolates scopes through modules and explicit import lists with aliasing and qualified names.
